answer:
At 100 bar (10 MPa) and 37 °C (310.15 K), CO2 has a density of about **683.4 kg/m³** (0.683 g/cm³).

Two sources give the same number:
- **CoolProp** (Span–Wagner reference equation of state): 683.40 kg/m³.
- **NIST WebBook** (fetched live): 683.403 kg/m³.

At this point CO2 is supercritical. The critical point is 304.13 K and 73.77 bar, so it is just above the critical temperature. Close to the critical point the density changes sharply with T and P, by tens of kg/m³ per few degrees or bar, so small input errors matter. A cubic EOS such as Peng–Robinson can be noticeably off here, so use the reference equation (CoolProp or NIST). I did not compute the Peng–Robinson value.
